mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of UNRATE > 5.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in manufacturing and construction, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% while the federal funds rate remains above 4.5% signals disinflation under restrictive policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL < 102 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) above 0.4% signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumer spending and supports corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS monthly change > 0.4%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS decreases by > 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases by > 0.2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1% signals a sharp contraction in consumer spending, which directly reduces corporate revenues and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS monthly change < -1%.
